content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built and launched **Nestmark**, a responsive bookmark manager.

Features include:

- Add, edit, delete, archive, and favorite bookmarks
- Search, sorting, tags, and filtered collections
- Grid and list views
- Browser-local persistence
- Responsive desktop/mobile navigation
- Keyboard shortcut: `⌘/Ctrl + K` for search

Verified the key flows and production build with no browser console errors.

Open it at **http://maker:4000**.

Nestmark looks lovely, and I can see it does a lot of what I need — I can save links, tag them, favorite them, tuck things into the archive, search, and switch between the grid and list views. That part feels good and I'm happy with how it all looks and moves.

There's one thing that's core to how I imagined saving, though. When I hit "Add bookmark," it asks me to type in the title and description myself. What I really want is to just paste in a web address and have the app go grab the page's name and its little summary (and its icon) for me automatically — so saving a link is basically one step. Right now if I leave the title blank it just uses the website's address as the name, which isn't the same thing.

Could you make it so that pasting a URL pulls in the page's title and description on its own? That's the piece I'd want fixed before I'd call the saving flow done. Everything else I've tried here is working well for me.

content:
Implemented the automatic bookmark enrichment flow.

Now, after pasting a URL, Nestmark automatically fetches:

- Page title
- Meta description
- Website icon
- Canonical URL when available

The Save button waits for the lookup to finish, while all populated fields remain editable. Sites that block metadata access still fall back gracefully to manual entry.

Verified against Example Domain and MDN, including persistence after reload. The updated app is available at **http://maker:4000**.

That's exactly what I was after. I tried adding a link and pasting in a web address, and Nestmark went and pulled in the page's name and its summary on its own — I checked it with Example Domain and it filled in the title and description for me, with the fields still editable in case I want to tweak them, and the Save button holding until it's done. That's the one-step saving I wanted, and if a site won't share its details I can still type them in myself.

Everything else I'd tried before is still working nicely — saving, tagging, favoriting, archiving, searching, and clicking through to the original links. This does what I set out to build. I'm happy with it.
